Book CLUB

without identity?

What is a book club

without

identity?

Imagine a place where you gather with folk who appreciate the same activity as you, value the great amount of communication about it as you and share the same passion for it as you. Well, that place for a bookworm certainly is a book club. Or at least for a bookworm that knows for a certain book club existance.


Book clubs, after all, only exist if the bookworms know about them. And Odense International Book Club has missed a visual form in which they could present their existance, yet their bookworms worked hard around it to find their vision and present the club to other potential bookworms.

bookclub’s

voice

The book club’s identity was created to express its character and values while building a sense of readers connection.


Through the identity I developed, the book club was able to present itself at an event, communicate its character, and attract more than 50 new members.


Highlighting storytelling is the most important part of this journey. Additionally, inspiring the demonstration of how thoughtful identity design can spark curiosity, strengthen an organisation, and bring people together around a shared love of reading.


Odense International Book Club is now a place with identity and around 1000 members.

← Storytelling

Odense International Book Club

Without identity?

01 / The idea

What is a book club without identity?

Imagine a place where you gather with people who appreciate the same activity, enjoy discussing it, and share your passion. For a bookworm, that place is a book club.

Odense International Book Club needed a visual identity to share its existence and invite new readers into the community.

02 / Values and visuals

Values and visuals

The club brings people together around classic books translated into English, sharing readers’ opinions and impressions over a warm drink. The first sketch was designed to reflect these values.

03 / Color palette

Color palette

Warm book tones and thoughtful, intelligent discussions shape the club’s visual palette.

  • #FFE1BD
  • #261E17
  • #BD6908
  • #662028
  • #2F4731

04 / Imagery style

Imagery style

The artwork respects the chosen colors while expressing the book club’s classic, moody, and mystical character.

05 / Event and presentation

Bringing the identity to life

The club presented its activities at an International Days event in Odense’s Main Library. Printed materials gave the identity a voice and helped introduce the club to new readers.

06 / Effect today

A community with a voice

A planned, structured identity made a difference: the club could communicate its character, attract more than 50 new members at an event, and grow to around 1,000 members.

Books bring people together.

Thoughtful identity design can spark curiosity, strengthen an organisation, and bring people together around a shared love of reading.
